[[File:Suqah icon.png|left]]
'''Suqahs''' are a race of strange-looking but powerful creatures native to [[Lunar Isle]]. Players must have at least started [[Lunar Diplomacy]] to have access to Lunar Isle. Despite their fearsome nature, they have a peaceful relationship with the [[Moon Clan]] (which gave magic to them to protect themselves according to the [[Oneiromancer]]), but are aggressive to outsiders, effectively serving as guards.

A suqah will try to attack with melee, even at a distance. Those on the northern part of the isle attack with melee and a weak version of [[Ice Barrage]] or [[Water Wave]] on their opponents. The Ice Barrage attack always only freezes the player for about five seconds -  it is still possible to fight or eat while frozen, but not possible to walk or run.

Suqahs on the southern portion of the island do not use Ice Barrage, making them the more common target for [[Slayer assignments]]. However, these suqahs are more widespread and, therefore, less efficient for the use of a [[dwarf multicannon]]. Though it is more costly due to the necessity of extra food or [[prayer potion]]s required for Protect From Magic, killing the suqahs on the northern portion of the island with a dwarf multicannon drastically speeds up Slayer tasks. When wearing a [[twisted bird skull necklace]]/[[split dragontooth necklace]]/[[demon horn necklace]] along with a [[bonecrusher]] and a dwarf multicannon, players will regain [[prayer points]] very fast.

A caged suqah is on the bottom deck of Captain Bentley's ship, the ''[[Lady Zay]]'', docked on Lunar Isle, which attacks with magic but only when the door is open; therefore, it can be ranged/maged/halberded in complete safety. Note that this suqah will not appear when the ship is docked at the [[Pirates' Cove]].

Suqahs mainly drop [[Suqah tooth|suqah teeth]] or [[herbs]], and rarely drop anything else. Suqah teeth can be sold to the [[tooth fairy]] for 2,000 coins each after [[A Fairy Tale III - Battle at Ork's Rift]]. Suqah teeth are also one of the five components needed to get the [[tooth creature]].

==Update history==
{{UH|
* {{UL|type=update|update=Patch Notes: Part 2 - Combat Style Modernisation|date=2 March 2026}}
** Default base hit chances increased:
*** Magic ('weak'): 65 → 70
*** Melee ('same'): 55 → 60
*** Ranged ('strong'): 45 → 50

* {{UL|type=ninja|update=This Week In RuneScape - 26/10/20#Patch Notes|date=26 October 2020}}
** Monsters with multiple variants will now consistently spawn as those variants when newly placed in the [[Sunken Pyramid|Personal Slayer Dungeon]].
*** This includes suqah.

* {{UL|type=patch|update=Patch Notes (23 October 2017)|date=23 October 2017}}
** Several suqah spawn locations have been moved to tiles accessible to players.

* {{UL|type=ninja|update=Patch Notes (25 April 2016)|date=25 April 2016}}
** Improved respawn rates for suqahs.

* {{UL|type=patch|update=Patch Notes (5 May 2015)|date=5 May 2015}}
** Suqahs will no longer use melee attacks from a distance.

* {{UL|type=patch|update=Patch Notes (8 July 2009)|date=8 July 2009}}
** Suqahs now drop [[charm]]s more consistently.

* {{UL|type=update|update=Lunar Diplomacy|date=24 July 2006}}
** Added to game.
}}

==Trivia==
* Suqahs appear to be capable of hitting players at a distance with their melee attacks. It is unknown whether or not this is a glitch.
* Their appearance and attacking animation were updated along with the [[Livid Farm]] update.
